info.title: AI Platform API
info.description: OpenAPI schema for AI Platform workspace service

post.description: ADMIN ONLY. The gate lives in the REST handler this delegates to.

ADMIN ONLY. Rebuilds the REST body preserving which fields were SET, so an
omitted field stays unchanged rather than being cleared.
UNAUTHENTICATED because the inference key is the credential.

BillingLine.title: BillingLine
BillingLine.description:
One model's share of a bill.

`priced` is per-line and not derived from the amount: an unpriced model must
render "not yet priced", never a zero that reads as free.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.default: Preview — usage-based estimate, not an invoice.

CatalogBillingResponse.title: CatalogBillingResponse
CatalogBillingResponse.description:
Showback for one tenant, one line per model.

A single total is no longer enough: one key now spans every listed model, so
a tenant that cannot see which model spent the money cannot act on the
number. `partial` means at least one line is unpriced, so the total is a
floor and not the bill.

CatalogCapabilitiesResponse.title: CatalogCapabilitiesResponse
CatalogCapabilitiesResponse.description:
Advisory: what the caller may do in the catalog.

Lets the console state the admin gate up front rather than letting a tenant
fill in a listing form and only then be refused. Purely presentational —
the commands re-check, so this grants nothing.

CatalogListingCard.title: CatalogListingCard
CatalogListingCard.description:
The descriptive card an admin attaches when listing a model.

Context window and region were dropped from this surface: both were free
text an admin retyped per listing, so they were authored once and then went
stale against the thing they described -- the context window in particular
is a property of the running engine, which already reports it and refuses
an over-long prompt with the real number. The columns remain in the table,
unwritten, so restoring them is a schema-free change if they come back as
derived values rather than typed ones.

ConsumerUsageRow.title: ConsumerUsageRow
ConsumerUsageRow.description: Admin view: one tenant's consumption of one listed model.

InferenceConfigurationOptionResponse.title: InferenceConfigurationOptionResponse
InferenceConfigurationOptionResponse.description:
A deployment recipe as an option a tenant can actually choose.

`name`, `model_family` and `serving_pattern` are here because the create form
cannot work without them, and this DTO is the only answer it gets: the picker
labels each row `name · serving_pattern`, submits the `name` as the recipe,
and filters the list to recipes whose `model_family` matches the chosen model
(a Qwen model listing `deepseek-pd` is an option create would then reject).
Projected away, every row renders blank and none of them can be selected —
the whole deploy flow stops at an empty dropdown.

main's reduction dropped them because main had no recipe picker to serve.
They disclose nothing this response does not already: `default_configuration`
is published in full right below, and it carries `command`, `model_path` and
`env`. A recipe's own name is strictly less than that.

InferenceConfigurationPreviewResponse.title: InferenceConfigurationPreviewResponse
InferenceConfigurationPreviewResponse.description:
Read-only preview of the configuration a create would deploy.

Exactly one field: the resolved configuration, already passed through the
same positive public allowlist as the instance DTOs. The internal result also
carries the operator-complete configuration used for rollback; none of it is
projected here.

InferenceInvocationResponse.title: InferenceInvocationResponse
InferenceInvocationResponse.description:
One relayed call to the public OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

`response` is the upstream body verbatim -- it is the caller's own inference
result, not platform state. `upstream_status` is preserved separately because
the control-plane envelope always answers 200; without it a caller cannot
tell a rejected API key (401/403) from a model error.

InferenceKeyPublicResponse.title: InferenceKeyPublicResponse
InferenceKeyPublicResponse.description:
Metadata for one tenant API key. Never the token.

`tenant_id` is dropped: the route is tenant-scoped, so it can only ever echo
the caller's own tenant back at it.

The expiry is published as `valid_until` rather than `expires_at`.
`expires_at` is on the reviewed contract's prohibited list because it names a
reader lease's internal liveness deadline; a credential's own expiry is
genuinely user-facing -- a user cannot rotate a key whose end date it cannot
see -- so it is published under a name that is not the banned one.

`scoped_instances` is Optional and NOT defaulted to []: None means an
unscoped, tenant-wide key that calls every model, while [] is an empty
allowlist that authorizes nothing. Collapsing the two would invert the
meaning of the most permissive key in the system.

InferenceKeyRevocationResponse.title: InferenceKeyRevocationResponse
InferenceKeyRevocationResponse.description:
Acknowledgement that a key was revoked.

The revoke route used to answer with a bare `dict`, which publishes no schema
at all. This mirrors the `*ActionResponse` shape the other domains use, keyed
by the same `lookup_id` the caller passed in.

InferenceKeyScopeResponse.title: InferenceKeyScopeResponse
InferenceKeyScopeResponse.description:
One deployment a key is restricted to, resolved for display.

`stale` is not cosmetic: deleting and recreating a deployment mints a new
instance id while the stored scope still names the old one, so the key
silently authorizes nothing. A bare id list would render an expired grant as
though it still worked.

InferenceLogsPublicResponse.title: InferenceLogsPublicResponse
InferenceLogsPublicResponse.description:
Container logs for one deployment, read through the backend.

Field-for-field the same as the internal DTO, because every field on it is
already user data: there is no attempt timeline, no namespace, no pod name
and no dashboard url to strip. `degraded` is load-bearing -- without it an
empty `logs` cannot be told apart from "the log store was unreachable", and a
UI would report "no logs" for an outage.

InferenceMetricsPublicResponse.title: InferenceMetricsPublicResponse
InferenceMetricsPublicResponse.description:
Live serving metrics for one deployment.

`pools` arrives already reduced by `project_public_inference_pools` (role,
ready, desired, live, status) -- images, argv, env, mounts, probes and
networking never reach this DTO. The `grafana_*_url` fields are expiring,
tenant-scoped embed tickets minted server-side after ownership is proven.
Null means "not configured", which a UI renders as no link rather than a
dead one.

InferenceOperationPublicResponse.title: InferenceOperationPublicResponse
InferenceOperationPublicResponse.description:
Progress of one accepted lifecycle operation.

`fence_token` and `lease_expires_at` are dropped: both belong to the worker
lease that fences concurrent reconcilers, and neither is actionable by the
caller. `revision_id` stays because it is the join back to
GetInferenceRevision -- it is what makes "which change is this?" answerable.

InferenceRevisionPublicResponse.title: InferenceRevisionPublicResponse
InferenceRevisionPublicResponse.description:
One immutable desired-state revision.

`spec_digest`, `artifact_manifest_digest` and `controller_kind` are dropped.
The two digests are reconciliation bookkeeping -- the tracker compares them
to decide whether to re-apply -- and `controller_kind` names the Kubernetes
object (Deployment vs LeaderWorkerSet) that renders the revision, which is
the same class of fact as `deployment_name`. `effective_spec` is already
reduced to the tenant-visible launch knobs by the internal DTO's validator.

InferenceRuntimeConfigPublicResponse.title: InferenceRuntimeConfigPublicResponse
InferenceRuntimeConfigPublicResponse.description:
ADMIN-ONLY: the image, env and engine flags a deployment actually runs.

This is the ONE published operation that deliberately exposes operator state,
and it is the reviewed exception rather than a widening of the tenant
projection: the REST handler it delegates to requires catalog-admin before
anything is read. Everything here is already reachable by that same admin
through the runtime-config PATCH, so reducing the read while leaving the
write open would only make the surface harder to reason about. It is
published under /api/v1/ because the console's admin panel is an ordinary
tenant client that happens to hold the admin claim.

InferenceRuntimePoolPublicResponse.title: InferenceRuntimePoolPublicResponse
InferenceRuntimePoolPublicResponse.description:
One serving pool's live container identity, as published.

Mirrors the internal model field-for-field on purpose: the public contract is
fail-closed, so an unlisted field is dropped rather than forwarded. Adding a
field to the internal DTO alone silently publishes nothing.

Live container ENV is absent here for the same reason it is absent
internally -- it can carry provider tokens and signed URLs, including ones no
current release knows to redact.

ListingPricing.title: ListingPricing
ListingPricing.description:
What a listing costs, straight from the price book in force.

Deliberately the same row that `rate_rollups` bills against (keyed by
`rate_key`), so the number a tenant is quoted before calling a model and the
number they are charged afterwards cannot drift apart.

`cached_input_price_per_million` is the cache-read rate. None means no
cached rate is in force, which bills cache hits at the full input rate --
not free. A listing with no price row at all yields `pricing=None`, which
the UI must render as "not yet priced" rather than as zero.

An all-zero block is a different answer from None and renders differently:
it is a price row an admin wrote, so the model really is free.

MintedInferenceKeyPublicResponse.title: MintedInferenceKeyPublicResponse
MintedInferenceKeyPublicResponse.description:
The one and only time the plaintext token exists.

`token` is public BY DESIGN and only here: the server stores a hash, so a key
that is not read from this response can never be recovered. `lookup_id` is
the durable handle used to list and revoke it.

ProblemResponse.title: ProblemResponse
ProblemResponse.description: RFC 7807 problem details returned by public APIs.

RequestEventResponse.title: RequestEventResponse
RequestEventResponse.description:
One ledger row. METADATA ONLY — no prompt or completion text exists in
this table, so none can be returned here even by mistake.

inference_instance_ids.title: Inference Instance Ids
inference_instance_ids.description: Restrict this key to these deployed inference instances. Omit for a tenant-wide key that calls every model.

username.title: Username
username.description: Free-text label for whoever this key is for, e.g. a person's username. Display only -- it grants nothing.

RpcUpdateInferenceRuntimeConfigRequest.title: RpcUpdateInferenceRuntimeConfigRequest
RpcUpdateInferenceRuntimeConfigRequest.description:
ADMIN-ONLY runtime edit, RPC shape.

Subclasses the REST body so the two cannot drift, and adds the id the RPC
envelope needs. The handler rebuilds a clean REST body with
`exclude_unset=True`: an omitted field must stay OMITTED, because the PATCH
treats omitted as unchanged and a blanked `env` would take a running
deployment down.

SetListingPricingRequest.title: SetListingPricingRequest
SetListingPricingRequest.description:
Admin: set the price for a listing, versioned by `effective_from`.

Writes a new price-book row rather than updating one. Rating joins usage to
the price in force at each bucket's own time, so a price change must never
rewrite what a tenant was already charged.

Everything defaults, and that is deliberate: this is also the block that
rides along with a listing, where an admin who types no numbers is saying
"this model is free" rather than leaving the price unknown. The default is
only safe because it is written as a REAL row -- a listing with no row at
all still means "not yet priced" and must never render as 0.

UpdateInferenceRuntimeConfigRequest.title: UpdateInferenceRuntimeConfigRequest
UpdateInferenceRuntimeConfigRequest.description:
ADMIN-ONLY runtime edit. Every field optional; omitted means unchanged.

Carries every member of OPERATOR_INFERENCE_CONFIGURATION_KEYS.
`command`/`args` are absent on purpose: argv belongs to the catalog recipe,
and a per-instance override would drift silently from the recipe every
future deploy is rendered from.

UsageSummary.title: UsageSummary
UsageSummary.description: Totals over the window, plus the honesty flags the UI must surface.

ValidateInferenceKeyPublicResponse.title: ValidateInferenceKeyPublicResponse
ValidateInferenceKeyPublicResponse.description:
Whether an API key is live, and whose it is labelled as.

Published verbatim rather than reduced: `tenant_id` is normally dropped from
a public DTO because a tenant-scoped route can only echo the caller's own
tenant back, but this route is UNAUTHENTICATED and has no caller tenant --
identifying the key's tenant is the entire purpose.

`tenant_id` and `username` are populated only when `valid` is true; every
failure answers with the bare `{"valid": false}` so the endpoint cannot be
used to tell a real key from an unknown one.
